reviews.comment: Wonderful, sweet, and obviously brilliant man, but unfortunately not a good professor. No one ever showed up to class because he would ramble on for an hour and a half about irrelevant tangents. I had to teach myself the entire class. The only advantage is that the tests are exactly like the practice exams. That being said, he is a very kind man.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Naugle does not know how to teach physics. Period. The scarce number of examples that were done in the lecture were complex and you could not understand a word of what this man was saying. Your exams, with exception of the final, are written by Dr. Ford, so if anything, do not go to Don's class, but Dr. Ford's. The final is significantly harder
Very hard. Helpful but doesn't know much about the subject.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Brilliant man, awful professor. Naugle probably should have retired 5-10 years ago for the sake of everyone. His Q drop rate is over double that of the other professors for a reason. His most recent curve of 5 points when the class average was a 35 so there's that. Take Ford if at all possible.

Sitting through the lectures made me want to jump off Rudder. He is smart in his own head but the lectures were extremely confusing because of the algebraic mistakes. There were even a few lectures on stuff not pertaining to tests. He is a very nice guy and is willing to help outside of class, he is just terrible at lecturing. Work hard to get an A

Naugle's lectures are extremely non-helpful and you have to rely on recitation and your own study habits to succeed in the class. I rarely actually took notes during the lectures because none of it was helpful.  He is a really smart and nice guy but his teaching techniques are not all there.

If taking PHYS 218: You will learn absolutely nothing in this class. Naugle's lectures are weak and insufficient; HE IS A HORRIBLE TEACHER. There is absolutely no homework. You must teach yourself via textbook, or you will fail the course, guaranteed. The only grades in the class are the occasional  one question clicker quizzes and the four exams.

Donald Naugle, while a very smart man, does not know how to teach an entry-level physics course. I've sat in on many other lecturers this semester, and my words of advice are to pick any of them. Avoid Dr. Naugle at all costs for low-level courses.

Naugle was not a very good teacher at all. Had the worst averages out of all the "don't panic" sections.  However his bright and smiling face is the only thing that keeps me from jumping off the top of the Mitchell Physics Building, ending my miserable life.  Help me. Physics is hard in general but I would find a different professor.

He is legitimately a nice guy. However, he doesn't really teach physics and instead just proves the fundamental theorem of calculus during every class. I already know physics and sat in the lecture just for fun. It was extremely confusing.

He made mistakes very often. So many mistakes that it got to the point that the students themselves were teaching the class and simultaneously teaching Donald Naugle himself. The class's lectures get nothing really done since half of the time it was just proving already proven concepts with no relevance to our curriculum. Overall, a thumbs down.
